newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Sleet drives Hungary BCE wheat prices up.
newsitem.headline: Sleet drives Hungary BCE wheat prices up.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices rose by the 400-forint limit for all maturities in the grain section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange as a reaction to the sleet that might jeopardise the crop, traders said on Friday.
"Although the weather is too cold for sleet to have a real effect on wheat it was a natural market reaction," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
Sleet can form an ice cover under which wheat can rot.
Another reason for the price rise was a speculative move of one brokerage, he added.
"They had 50-lot buy offers 400 forints higher for March and May, probably because they intend to sell next week," Szoke said.
Milling wheat prices closed at 28,520 forints, up 400 for May, the only traded maturity.
Maize prices remained steady except for May which went up by 100 forints to end at 19,800, but Szoke expected last year's downward trend to continue eventually.
Feed barley prices rose by 200 to 400 forints and Szoke said they could rise further.
"The planted area was small and this is bound to be reflected in prices as well," he said.
Turnover was a meagre 132.7 million forints or 285 lots, of which 167 were maize, 113 milling wheat and five feed wheat contracts.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
